content.content:
Opening a draft writes that draft's record last: after the draft's workspace exists and its base is captured, and not before (szvotxpq). The surface already fixes what opening writes — for each named node a workspace, a record in the state `open`, and a report of the handle and the path — and it stops short of fixing where a failure leaves them, putting what a failed workspace creation or record write leaves behind outside itself (szvotxpq). That reserved question is the one this decision answers, and it answers it with order rather than with a cleanup: the record is the last of the writes, so an open that fails leaves no record naming a workspace (rqtowtqn).

The record waits on the workspace because the record names it. A record carries the draft's workspace as a reference, and the path that reference gives is derived from the record's handle and from nothing else, so the reference is a claim about exactly one directory: that the draft's working copy is there (xqzstoyo). The surface makes the same directory the draft's place, since each draft is written in its own workspace (szvotxpq), so a record written earlier would name a place where the draft is not. And what is named is not a path that has merely been made: the workspace is the surface's own creation (szvotxpq) and a working copy of the repository's tree, a checkout of the repository's own content (xqzstoyo). The decision therefore names the workspace and the base as two conditions because a directory can be made while a working copy is not, though they arrive together — a workspace that exists as a working copy has the base it was checked out at, and until that base is captured the directory holds nothing of the tree the draft is to change.

The record comes last because “no record survives” has a fixed meaning in the store. A record is exactly one JSON document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, named by the handle, and stored records are enumerated only by scanning that directory (rqtowtqn). Nothing else holds the list: there is no index to walk back, no second file to clear, and a handle the directory does not name is a record that is not there (rqtowtqn). So the order is the whole of the guarantee, not half of one: a failed open has no record write to undo, because the one document that could be found is written after the thing it would be found to name.

Read back, the order gives the registry two properties, and both are read off the same scan. A draft the CLI did not finish creating is not in the list, because its document is not in the directory — whatever a failed workspace creation or base capture left on disk, no record names it (rqtowtqn, szvotxpq). And every record the directory does name is a draft whose workspace and base the CLI finished creating, because the surface gives each draft one record apiece and a record is written only after its workspace exists (szvotxpq, rqtowtqn). Stated from the workspace side, a workspace without a record is a directory the registry does not list — a workspace the CLI began and did not finish, not a draft — while a record whose workspace creation failed is the one state the order forbids (rqtowtqn).

The report the surface fixes follows the record rather than preceding it. It reports the record's own fields, the handle and the workspace path the handle derives, for each draft as it is opened (szvotxpq), so it is not issued for a draft whose record is not yet written: reporting a handle before writing the document that carries it would name a handle the directory does not name, which is a record that is not there (szvotxpq, rqtowtqn).

The rule is applied per draft, not per call. The list the surface takes is one draft per named node (szvotxpq), so a call naming three nodes opens three drafts and applies the order three times, once to each draft's own workspace, base and record. Nothing here orders the drafts of one call against each other, and nothing here settles what such a call does once one draft's open has failed or how the drafts it did open are reported.

These clauses are one commitment. The surface says what opening writes and reserves what a failure leaves behind (szvotxpq); the workspace node says the record names a directory the handle derives and that the workspace is a working copy rather than a directory (xqzstoyo); the store says the one document at the handle's name is the record and the scan is the only list (rqtowtqn). Put the record last and the three read as one statement: for each draft, the workspace and its base first, then the one document at the handle's name, then the report that names it — so a failed open leaves nothing the registry can find, and every record it can find names a draft the CLI finished creating. Write the record first and the registry would list drafts with no working copy; write it after a directory but before its base and the record would name a workspace the draft cannot be written in; leave any second trace of a failed open and the scan would no longer be the list. Each alternative breaks one of the three, and the order is the sequence that breaks none.

Deliberately not here: how a failed open's workspace is cleaned up — removed, reused or left — beyond the fact that no record survives it; the mechanism that makes the record write last, whether the order of calls, a temporary file or a rename; what a failed open prints, and which exit status it uses; whether a base-capture failure is distinguishable from a workspace-creation failure, and how a retry behaves; the order of the drafts of one call against each other; and what a missing workspace means once a record has been written, a question xqzstoyo already declines to decide. Each can change without touching the answer: for each draft the workspace and its base exist before the one record is written, and nothing the registry can look up names a draft the CLI did not finish creating.
content.rationale:
The surface puts one question outside itself, and this node is the answering of it. Opening a draft is already fixed (szvotxpq): one draft per named node, each in its own workspace, each record written in the state `open`, each handle and path reported, and nothing of the graph written — and the same document reserves what a failed workspace creation or record write leaves behind. Reserving it without settling it is not a gap another commitment will fill: a failed open is produced by this verb, so what it leaves is this verb's to fix, and no prerequisite in this layer claims it. The decision answers with the order of the verb's writes rather than with a cleanup, because order is the part of the failure path that is the verb's own: what is written is fixed by the store and where the workspace lives is fixed by the workspace node, so the only thing still open is when the record is written.

The workspace comes first because the record's content is a claim about it. A record carries the draft's workspace as a reference, and the reference is derived from the handle and from nothing else (xqzstoyo), so a reader holding the record and the handle expects one directory to hold the draft. A record written before that directory holds a working copy asserts something false: the surface makes the workspace the draft's place — each draft is written in its own workspace (szvotxpq) — and a place the draft is not in is not the draft's workspace. The condition is the working copy and its base together rather than the path, because xqzstoyo's workspace is a checkout of the repository's own content: a directory that has been made but not based holds nothing of the tree the draft is to change. Naming both is not a second condition bolted onto the first; it is what makes the first true, and it is why a directory that exists is not yet something a record may name.

The record is last because the store makes it decisive. There is one JSON document per record, named by the handle, at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, and the stored records are enumerated only by scanning that directory (rqtowtqn). With the list being the directory's contents there is no secondary state to keep in step, and a handle the directory does not name is a record that is not there (rqtowtqn). So “no record survives a failed open” is not a promise about an undo step; it is what never writing the document before the thing it names already means. That is why the decision does not choose between removing, reusing and leaving a failed workspace: the registry is clean by construction, and the workspace's fate is outside anything a scan can see.

The two properties the order buys are the two the surface's reservation names. No record names a failed draft's workspace, because the document is written after that workspace would have existed, so the report of handle and path is never issued for it. And no record the scan finds names a workspace the CLI did not finish creating, because the surface gives each draft one record apiece (szvotxpq) and every document's name resolves to a workspace and base made before it. A workspace without a record is therefore a started open rather than a draft, and the registry's list is exactly the set of drafts the verb finished opening — which is the surface's promise about what opening leaves behind, now with the failure case included.

What is not decided is left to the commitments that own it. The mechanism — the order of calls, a temporary file, a rename — is not named, because any of them that ends with one document at the handle's name satisfies the store's document and its discovery, and this decision is about which write is last, not how lastness is achieved. What a failed open prints and which exit status it uses are not decided here; the surface leaves printing and status to their own commitments, and no prerequisite in this layer fixes a message or a status. Whether a failed workspace is removed, and how a retry behaves, stay outside: a retry creates a workspace and a record by the same rule, and a removed workspace changes nothing the scan can see. What a missing workspace means after a record exists stays where xqzstoyo left it, since this decision fixes only the order that keeps that case from arising out of opening.

The form is inline prose (`text`) rather than one EARS requirement, because the commitment is an order read against three documents and carried by two consequences — the failing call and the registry's list — and each consequence needs its own licence clause by clause. The house reserves the single requirement sentence for decisions that reduce to one obligation; here the order, the workspace and base it waits on, and the scan that makes it decisive are three edges answering one question, and a sentence that dropped any of them would be satisfiable in a way the others forbid.
